newsitem.title: USA: Ohio manufacturers group opposes school fund plans.
newsitem.headline: Ohio manufacturers group opposes school fund plans.

text.p: An Ohio manufacturer's group said Wednesday it opposes the public school funding reform plans recommended by a state task force.

Ohio Manufacturers' Association also said it believes the state Supreme Court's March decision overturning the school funding system focused too much on money and not enough on quality, President Eric Burkland said.

Ohio lawmakers opened hearings this week in the Senate Finance Committee into the task force's recommendations to increase aid by $1.1 billion in the current biennium and provide $5.8 billion for capital improvements over the next 10 years.
"No one has demonstrated that billions of additional dollars will better prepare Ohio's public school children for the challenges of the workplace today or in the future," Burkland said.
Lawmakers must encourage competition, increase local involvement and provide longterm stable funding, Burkland said.

The association supports the task force plan to provide tax deductions for private school tuitions, but the proposals fail to address the need for fundamental changes in the tax structure, Burkland said.
Gov. George Voinovich's task force has recommended raising the state sales tax, the cigarette tax and property taxes on businesses and commercial properties to finance the spending.
The plan requires lawmakers to approve placing four constitutional amendments on the November ballot. Those referendums would have to be approved for placement by August 4.
